title: pane run --in <folder>: a Claude screen in an existing worktree
notes:
`pane run <id> --in <folder> "<prompt>"` starts a Claude screen in an existing folder or worktree.

Why: insta-experiences' main has dispatched every worker since 2026-11-09 by typing a terminal Claude Code into a claimed pane: `pane send "$id" "cd ../insta-experiences-net-prices && claude \"$(cat .prompt.txt)\""` (see its transcript 610a2bd2…, for example 2026-11-17T08:42). So its workers run as terminal Claude Code, not Claude screens: three of them run in panes 1:1–1:3 now. It does this because that project keeps its own worktrees on existing GitLab MR branches (insta-experiences-net-prices, -mr174, -tags), and `pane run` only runs in the project checkout, a --card worktree, or a fresh --worktree.

Want:
- `--in <folder>`: an existing directory, either inside the project or a worktree of the project's repository (`git worktree list` from the project). Refuse anything else with a reason, from one exported predicate (errors-rule-1). It excludes --card and --worktree. It makes and removes nothing: the folder is the caller's.
- The worker gets everything a normal run gets: a Claude screen (--terminal still works), the app's session settings, the report-to-main brief, scopes, and auto-close.
- Main's prompt and the pane usage name `--in` for an existing worktree, and say never to start Claude through `pane send`.
- Check the related report: insta main guards `case "$id" in 1:1|1:2|1:3) echo "refusing busy pane"`, which suggests `pane claim` handed out a pane running a terminal Claude Code started by `pane send`. Confirm whether paneIsBusy sees `claude` launched from the shell. Fix it if not, with a test.
- Decision modules with tests, Windows-safe. Docs (command, workers) and help change with it. Do not bump the version.

comments.body: Pull request #316 opened: pane run --in <folder>: a worker in an existing worktree https://github.com/naeemba/dashboard/pull/316

Converged, ready to merge. Review loop: 4 rounds, 12 findings fixed, 0 rejected (floor-addressed; the last-round nit, re-wrapping a comment in run-folder.ts, was fixed with no re-review after it). Merged main in first (board card conflict). CI then failed on windows: 5 run --in tests expected POSIX paths that path.resolve gives a drive letter on Windows. It had failed on every commit of the PR. Fixed in 9ba3731c by marking those tests posixPathsOnly, as ship.test.ts does. All 5 checks pass on head 9ba3731c.
